- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 70–75 range), then overshoot and fail to correct.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends — fails to recognize that prices often return to mid-range after peaks.
- Forecast horizon bias: 30d forecasts are overly optimistic in the short term (first 10 days) and overly pessimistic in the long term (last 10 days).
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — underestimates downward momentum.
- Model overfits recent high volatility — fails to smooth out noise in price history.
- Model ignores seasonal or calendar-based patterns (e.g., price dips around mid-month or after policy announcements).
- Model assumes linear continuation of recent trends — fails to account for sudden policy or market shocks.
- Model underestimates the impact of low volatility periods — fails to adjust downward when prices are consolidating.
- Model overestimates the persistence of recent highs — fails to recognize that prices often revert to 10–15% below peak within 10–15 days.
